issues.claim: The dossier cadence has three triggers in its producer and two in its home. V08 §3.6 (3) (l.1826-1840) folds an epoch at each year end, at each ± 5 % population crossing, 'and an epoch at the week of each newly carried calamity that no other epoch falls on (a destructive event is epoch content, §4.11's rung at an epoch)'. J-V8.55 (V08 l.3416) records this as citing '§4.11's cadence — … plus one at each new calamity's week'. §4.11 *The clock* (4) (l.8293-8299), the cadence's home, states only a 52-week boundary or a population move past the roster tolerance ('No epoch is folded per tick'). V06 §3.3.1 restates those two triggers (VAT2-r2-02), and `EpochInputs.events[].week` 'in (the previous epoch's week, week]' (l.8184) reads a calamity as riding the epoch whose span holds it. A port built from the home therefore folds a calamity of week 10 into the next year-end epoch, and while the dossier's present lies before that year end the calamity is not in the model at all. A port built from V08 folds it in its own week. Every reader of that epoch is affected: V06 §3.22 (1)'s aftermath, V06 §3.13 (2)'s hazard week, V04's burial deaths, and V01 §3.16 (2)'s disaster calamity read from 'the committed `epoch` events' (V01 l.2327-2330, l.343). At the present week of a fresh calamity no committed event holds it, so the look strikes the scatter pattern with no matched target, against item 122 (b)'s 'the calamity's `targets` win', and changes its units when the epoch later folds. The agreement matrix has no cadence row.
issues.required_change: §4.11 *The clock* (4): after 'by more than the **roster tolerance**, ± 5 % (J-A76.43; the one number §7.7 item 3's lapse reads too)' insert '— and at the week of each newly carried calamity that no other epoch falls on (DR28: a destructive event is epoch content; V08 §3.6 (3); J-V8.55)'. Keep the catch-up clause 'coarsened under item 119's comfort level by V06 §6.8 (6)'; a coarse catch-up carries a calamity in the coarse epoch that holds its week. V06 §3.3.1 states the same three triggers in the same round (VAT2-r2-02; R2-05).

issues.claim: V06 §3.3.1 (l.1073-1074) restates the port's cadence as '(a 52-week boundary, or a population move past the roster tolerance; …)'. V08 §3.6 (3) also folds an epoch at each newly carried calamity's week (VAT2-r2-01). V06 §3.22 (1)'s aftermath, 'in the epoch that holds its week', and V06's dossier-trace calamity row (l.388) read whichever cadence the port folds.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.3.1: replace '(a 52-week boundary, or a population move past the roster tolerance; a catch-up whose epochs at that cadence would pass the comfort level folds coarser, V06 §6.8 (6))' with '(a 52-week boundary, a population move past the roster tolerance, or a newly carried calamity's week, §4.11 *The clock* (4); a catch-up whose epochs at that cadence would pass the comfort level folds coarser, V06 §6.8 (6), a calamity then riding the coarse epoch that holds its week)'.

issues.claim: 'The creation week' has two meanings, and the first epoch's span reads it. (1) The present: §4.11 *The clock* (1) (l.8275-8276) says 'Its creation week is the present week of the dossier it is created from; a standalone map starts at week 0'. V06 §3.20.3 (l.3117) takes `W_p` as 'the present — the document's creation week (§4.11 *The clock* (1))', and V06 l.409 and EP-15 (l.8801, 'a replay starting 300 years before a week-0 creation') use the same meaning. (2) The first model's week: a history-first document's `generate` event stands at `W_p − round(52 × start.yearsAgo)` (V06 §3.20.3). V06 §2.11's `HistoryIndex.creationWeek` (l.809) is 'the week of the log's first model: a replayed document's first replay epoch's start', and V06 §3.15.2's `locate` (l.2317-2319) and §3.15.4's bar (l.2352) read that meaning. The span: `EpochInputs.years` is '(week − the previous epoch's week, or the creation week) ÷ 52' (l.8182), and V06's `ProductEpochContext.prevWeek` (l.467) and V06 §3.1 (3) (l.953-955) say the same. Under the home's definition the first replay epoch's `years` is (W_p − 52·toYearsAgo₁ − W_p) ÷ 52, which is below 0. Every per-year chance `1 − (1 − p)^years` (§4.11 *The clock* (5)) and every churn cap scaled by `years` then runs on a negative span. Under V06 §2.11's meaning, `years` is the first epoch's span.
issues.required_change: §4.11 *The clock* (1): replace 'Its creation week is the present week of the dossier it is created from; a standalone map starts at week 0.' with 'Its present at creation is the dossier's present week (a standalone map's, week 0). Its **creation week** — the week of its `generate` event, its first model's — is that present, except on a history-first document, whose `generate` event stands at the replay's start, `W_p − round(52 × start.yearsAgo)` (V06 §3.20.3); the first epoch's `prevWeek` and `years` (above) read the creation week, and a replayed past lies between it and the present.' In EP-15 (l.8801), 'before a week-0 creation' reads 'before a week-0 present'. V06's end is VAT2-r2-04 (R2-05).

issues.claim: V06 uses the present meaning of 'the creation week' in two places, against its own §2.11 (`HistoryIndex.creationWeek`, the replay's start), §3.15.2 and §3.15.4 (VAT2-r2-03): l.409, 'a replayed past lies before the creation week, V06 §3.20.3'; and §3.20.3 (l.3117), '`W_p` the present — the document's creation week (§4.11 *The clock* (1))'.
issues.required_change: V06 l.409: 'a replayed past lies before the creation week, V06 §3.20.3' → 'a replayed past lies between the creation week and the present, V06 §3.20.3'. V06 §3.20.3: '`W_p` the present — the document's creation week (§4.11 *The clock* (1)) —' → '`W_p` the present at creation (§4.11 *The clock* (1): the dossier's present week, a standalone document's week 0) —'. In the same paragraph, after 'the `generate` event stands at `W_p − round(52 × start.yearsAgo)`', add '— the document's creation week (`HistoryIndex.creationWeek`, V06 §2.11), which the first replay epoch's `prevWeek` and `years` read (V06 §3.1 (3))'.

issues.claim: V06 gives the decay level of a building the history replay ruined two readings. The default age: V06 §3.23 (4) (l.3381-3386) gives 'a building generated `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined`, or first met so in item 113's replay', V11's default age `D` under 'No decay run in the log'; T-V6-76 (d) (l.4081) bars 'H-HISTORY's ruins first met in the replay, read V11's default age'; V06 §3.21's decay row (l.3253) says the same. The replay's ops: the replay ruins and abandons buildings by ops of its epochs. V06 §3.20.5 (2) states 'every building `ruin`ed' at the destruction epoch's `hazards` step, and its decline and hazards act likewise. Those ops are lifecycle events of the creation prefix at known weeks (V06 §2.11's `HistoryIndex.epochs` with `replay: true`; `EffectiveWeek`). The decay run: by V06 §3.23 (1) these events start a decay run, and (5) reads 'a replay epoch's (a negative week is read as any week) — so scrubbing the history shows one plan aging (item 123 (a))'. V06 §3.21's combination row 'ruined plans × the history' (l.3283) gives 'the replay's ruins at their replayed years'. So a destruction two centuries before the present draws at `D`'s level under (4) and T-V6-76 (d), and at its state's top under (1) and §3.21's row; and under the default age a scrub of the replayed past shows no aging, against item 123 (a). R2-38 (3)'s rule, the default age 'for a building with no abandonment epoch', is unchanged; its example 'first met in item 113's replay' fits no building whose ruin the replay's own ops made. V03 §3.11 (c)'s as-built plan for such a building concerns the plan, not the level: the replay derives no plan.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.23 (4): 'A building generated `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined`, or first met so in item 113's replay,' → 'A building generated `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined` — its log holding no event that took it there from a standing state —'. After that sentence add: 'A building item 113's replay abandons or ruins (its decline, its hazards, V06 §3.20.5's destruction epoch) has its decay run in the creation prefix from that replay epoch's week ((1), (5)), so the present and every scrubbed week show its replayed years (item 123 (a)).' T-V6-76 (d) → 'a building generated ruined reads V11's default age; H-HISTORY's ruins read the years since the replay epoch that ruined them, a scrub across the replayed past showing each plan aging'. V06 §3.21's decay row: 'a building generated ruined or first met so in the replay | … V11's default age' → 'a building generated ruined | V11's default age; one the replay ruined | its replayed years'. The same correction in the same round (R2-05) at §2.6 step 7's parenthetical '(generated ruined; first met in item 113's replay)' (model) and at V11 §3.25.10's `settings` row ('one first met so in item 113's replay') (V11).

issues.claim: V06 §3.23 (4) (l.3381-3384) gives a building with no decay run in the log 'its state at V11's default age `D`: (2) with `w − A = 52 × D`'. That holds `w − A` constant at every week. A ruin generated at creation therefore reads the same level at creation and after a century of epochs, so its damage never accumulates. This is against item 123 (b) ('the decay level (0–1, from its existence state and the years since it was abandoned …) … Damage therefore only accumulates as decay goes on') and against V06 §3.23 (2)'s 'Years only add'. V11 §3.25.10's `settings` ('the years a building whose log holds no decay run reads at') and §2.6 step 7 read the same frozen age. Only the reading before V06's E2 lands, the existence state alone, has no clock to age by.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.23 (4): 'reads its state at V11's default age `D`: (2) with `w − A = 52 × D`' → 'reads its state as a decay run begun `D` years (V11's default age) before the week it was first met so — `A` = the creation week, the week of its `generate` event (§4.11 *The clock* (1)), − 52 × `D` — so it reads `D` years at creation and ages by (2) from then on as any run'. Keep 'Every reader reads every building so until this volume's E2 lands (M6-E): the existence state alone at V11's default age'. V06 §3.21's decay row and T-V6-76 (d) add 'a ruin generated at creation read after 50 years of epochs: `D` + 50 years, non-decreasing'. V11 §3.25.10's `settings` row reads 'the years such a building reads at the week it is first met' (V11; R2-05).

issues.claim: V07 drops the protected dwelling's exception at desertion. V07 §3.12 *Decline and desertion* (l.2542-2543) reads 'A deserted village — a target below 1, or no household left — is an outcome …: every dwelling vacates and decays over the dwell bands', and T-V7-16 (l.3615) bars 'a target of 0 vacates every dwelling'. The village's decline is V06's engine (V07 l.2505: 'the engine's strike lottery (V06 §3.5)'). V06 §3.5.1 (5) (l.1236-1238) never vacates a locked or pinned building: its last household 'lets out by a `relet` down to 0, the building keeping its state (§7.7's precedence)'. R2-18 (a) words the same exception at §2.6's clamp, §4.11 step (c), `LadderOp.relet` and §5.3's capacity row (l.9037). A deserted village holding a locked or pinned dwelling is therefore vacated by V07's statement and its bar, and kept by the engine's rule; T-V7-16 fails on a fixture that holds one.
issues.required_change: V07 l.2542-2543: 'every dwelling vacates and decays over the dwell bands' → 'every dwelling vacates and decays over the dwell bands — a locked or pinned dwelling excepted, whose last household leaves by a `relet` down to 0, the building keeping its state (V06 §3.5.1 (5); §7.7's precedence)'. T-V7-16: 'a target of 0 vacates every dwelling' → 'a target of 0 vacates every dwelling but a locked or pinned one, which keeps its state with 0 households (V06 §3.5.1 (5))'.

issues.claim: V02 and V03 call `crisisLookYields` for a preview, which V06 never defines. V02 §5.7 (1) (l.3028-3032) draws a disaster preview over a building 'while the building stands in a unit the look strikes and has not handed over ((6))', and (6) reads V06's `crisisLookYields(doc, building, overlay, week)` against 'the condition's `sinceWeek`'. V03 §5.6 (4) (l.2712-2717) applies the same 'not yet handed over' test to 'a `disaster` preview at §10.2's `previewSeverity`'. V06 §3.22 types `overlay: Id /* a ConditionOverlay whose look ruins the building */`, and its rule reads the overlay's `sinceWeek`. A preview has no overlay and no `sinceWeek` (V06 §3.22 (1): 'A crisis preview … has no condition and no aftermath'; V01 §3.16 passes `null` for one). So whether a previewed ruin yields to a building's running repair or rebuild Works is undefined, and the two callers pass a value the callee does not take.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.22's signature reads `overlay: Id | null /* null: a preview */`. Its (3) adds: 'A preview (`overlay` null) never hands over: `crisisLookYields` is false for it, so a previewed ruin draws over every building of its units whatever their Works, and ends with the preview'. V06 §3.21's hand-over row adds 'a preview over a building under a rebuild Works | the look drawn (a preview never hands over)'. V02 §5.7 (1) and V03 §5.6 (4) cite it (R2-05).
